rationale: The work cleanly enacts Bochner's gesture in the browser: the page is the measurement of its own container, redrawn on every resize. Concept and execution collapse (P1): the dimension lines are not decoration, they are the work. The double-coding is solid — casual viewer sees the gag, literate viewer reads the conceptual-art claim. Ethics are stated and met. It is materially distinct from the catalogue: la-trahison-des-images stretches an image, this way browser sums pointer travel, and no existing work measures the viewport itself.
reservations: Novelty is moderate rather than high: the Bochner-to-viewport transposition is legible and well-executed but not especially surprising; the chance/order axis is acknowledged but chance barely enters (only via the visitor's device). The wall-label text in the center slightly undercuts the 'nothing but the measurement' claim — it is a small P3 restraint issue. Wit is dry but not particularly sharp.
revision_suggestion: Consider removing or shrinking the central label so the page truly contains only the dimension lines, tightening P3. A subtler way to introduce chance (e.g., a second measurement in a unit the visitor didn't choose, or a brief flicker on resize) would deepen the P5 axis without breaking the order of the piece.
